speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing episodes of unresponsiveness accompanied by facial grimacing; can you tell me exactly how long these episodes typically last and whether you lose consciousness completely?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Childhood Absence Epilepsy (Note: The 3-4 minute duration and post-ictal lethargy described by the patient are atypical for classic absence seizures, which usually last <15 seconds and lack post-ictal confusion; the clinical picture of staring, automatisms/hand gestures, and a "muddy taste" is more suggestive of complex partial seizures or focal impaired awareness seizures with secondary generalization, possibly with a focal onset such as temporal or frontal lobe etiology).
